executive_summary: Your RED status is driven almost entirely by supplier concentration in China and geopolitical flash points—six of eleven critical/high-risk suppliers sit in China (Huizhou BYD, Smoore, Porton, IP Sun, EVE Energy) and are all flagged for recent military buildup signals, plus you have critical exposure in two of them (Huizhou BYD and Smoore in EMS, a chokepoint category). Beyond China, India's ITC (high BAT exposure in nicotine) faces border tensions, and Finland's Stora Enso sits on the NATO-Russia frontier. The immediate action is dual: segment your China supply base by criticality and map alternative EMS and battery sourcing outside the region, since those two categories are your bottleneck; simultaneously, run war-game scenarios on what a Taiwan strait escalation or China-India border flare would mean for your 60–90 day fulfillment. AMCOR's stock drop and Texas Instruments' decline warrant quick calls to validate whether these are sector-wide moves or supplier-specific stress. The macro GREEN status won't save you if geopolitical risk crystallizes—this is a working-level sourcing and logistics problem, not a macroeconomic one.
